raw_response: Banks characterized their net charge-off levels as normalizing or trending toward pre-pandemic levels. Specifically, U.S. Bank expected full-year 2024 net charge-offs to be in the "mid-50s" basis points, noting that credit card charge-offs were getting closer to pre-pandemic levels but would continue to move up slightly. Capital One reported that its gross charge-offs were leveling off very close to 2018 and 2019 levels, while net charge-offs leveled off at a level approximately 15% above 2019 due to lower recoveries. Bank of America noted in Q2 2023 that the trend was moving toward pre-pandemic levels but remained below historical levels, with a charge-off rate of 33 basis points; by Q2 2024, the net charge-off ratio was 59 basis points, largely unchanged from the first quarter. M&T Bank stated in Q2 2024 that asset quality trends were performing as expected, with net charge-offs in line with their expectations and reductions in non-accrual and criticized balances.
